headline: Huafa redemption fears fade and the 1.25% overnight anchor goes live; 10Y CCDC eases to 1.634%
summary: CGBs sold off in the morning on worries about Huafa-linked fund redemptions, then rallied in the afternoon as buyers came back, led by the long end. The CCDC 10-year fell 1.6bp to 1.634% and the 30-year 1.7bp to 2.066%, with the 50-year down 2.4bp, while the 2-year eased only 0.9bp to 1.237%. Policy banks kept pace in 5–10Y: CDB 10-year fell 2.2bp to 1.671%, 3.7bp over CGB, with ADBC and EXIM about 6.7bp and 5.7bp over; CDB 2-year rose 0.8bp, so short policy bank spreads widened.
drivers: Friday's selloff came from pre-emptive redemptions of credit ETFs and bond funds after Zhuhai Huafa missed two trust repayments and sought bank loan extensions; Fitch put it on negative watch. Asset sales to Gree Group and Zhuhai Communications (RMB4.57bn) and steady wealth-product flows calmed nerves, so after a weak morning bank capital bonds and then CGBs drew buyers. Desks see no basis for a lasting selloff.

The PBOC ran its first daily fixed-rate overnight reverse repo, RMB541bn at 1.25%, against RMB1.056tn maturing, a RMB515bn net drain that the start of the month absorbed easily. Overnight Shibor slipped 0.3bp to 1.286% and 7-day 2.9bp to 1.363%. Funding at about 1.25–1.30% supports the 1–2Y but brings no new easing.
Weak official PMI vs strong RatingDog

The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 (forecast 50.0, prior 50.1), with new orders 49.4 and export orders 48.7, while the private RatingDog PMI held at 52.0, above the 51.6 forecast. Bonds leaned on the weak official print, which keeps the case for low yields intact.
Stock rebound and supply capped the rally

The Shanghai Composite rose 1.08% to 3,638 as the PBOC, NFRA and CSRC met banks and brokers about market support tools and buyback loans, which kept the 10-year from breaking lower. Demand at the policy bank auctions was strong (ADBC 10-year at 1.6566%, 7x covered), but government bond supply in Nov–Dec is still likely to exceed RMB1tn a month, including RMB150bn of special bonds for bank capital.
data: Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Private and export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and the case for continued easy funding.
Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Sep activity (Oct 19)
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
view: Neutral, leaning to buy dips, for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.61–1.66% CCDC range. The Huafa scare looks contained for now, the weak official PMI and funding near the 1.25% anchor support duration, and the 10-year still offers value against the rich 5–7Y belly. Against that, the stock market has official support, Nov–Dec supply is heavy and the PBOC treats the new rate as a framework change rather than a cut, so a break below 1.60% needs a fresh catalyst. I would stay long 10-year CGBs, underweight the belly and policy banks against CGBs, and neutral on the 30-year. Renewed redemptions or a Huafa default would push the 10-year back to 1.65–1.67%, while soft October trade, inflation or credit data could take it to 1.61%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 0.9bp to 1.237%, in the 6th percentile of its 1-year range (average 1.310%), and the 1-year at 1.168% sits about 12bp below overnight Shibor (1.286%). With the overnight anchor now live at 1.25%, the front end is pinned to funding and has little room to rally.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5-year eased 0.6bp to 1.348% and the 7-year 1.6bp to 1.444%, both in the 1st percentile of the year. 2s5s10s is −17.6bp (3rd percentile, average −7.5bp) and 5s7s10s −9.4bp, a 1-year low. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is open at 28.7bp (72nd percentile, average 26.4bp), slightly in the money and inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The long from 1.65% is 1.6bp in the money with the 10-year at 1.634%; the 1.665% add level was not reached. It stays cheap against its neighbours: the 7s10s20s fly is −23.6bp, in the 87th percentile against a −29.4bp average, even though the level is in the 1st percentile of the year.
buckets.call: Long from 1.65%, target 1.61%, stop 1.68%; add on a move to 1.665%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year fell 1.7bp to 2.066% and 10s30s is 43.2bp, in the 28th percentile and below its 45.6bp average. The 20-year at 2.061% trades almost flat to the 30-year, and the 30s50s spread has compressed to 12.2bp (8th percentile), so the ultra-long block has little cushion before heavy Nov–Dec supply. The 2.10% add level was not reached.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.7bp over CGB, in the 3rd percentile against a 9.9bp average, and the CDB 5-year spread is 9.6bp (2nd percentile). The CDB 2-year spread widened 1.7bp to 14.0bp (5th percentile) as short policy bank paper lagged. The switch from ~3bp is open and 0.7bp in the money.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.0bp more than CDB, in the 74th percentile against a 1.3bp average; EXIM is 2.0bp over, in line with its average. ADBC sold 10-year bonds at 1.6566% with 7x cover, so the pickup reflects supply and liquidity, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, still at a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 10.7bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp (17th percentile, average 12.7bp). Policy bank long bonds moved one for one with CGBs today, so the spread offers no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

cgb:1.note: Down 0.4bp to 1.168%; about 12bp below overnight Shibor as the 1.25% anchor went live.

cgb:2.note: Down 0.9bp to 1.237%, just below the new 1.25% overnight policy rate.

cgb:5.note: Down 0.6bp to 1.348%, near its 1-year low; still the richest point on the curve.

cgb:7.note: Down 1.6bp to 1.444%, a 1-year low, as buyers returned in the afternoon.

cgb:10.note: Down 1.6bp to 1.634%, retracing most of Friday's rise as Huafa fears faded.

cgb:30.note: Down 1.7bp to 2.066%; TL futures rose 0.31% as the long end led the rebound.

cdb:2.note: Up 0.8bp to 1.377%; about 14bp over CGB, wider by 1.7bp today.

cdb:5.note: Down 2.0bp to 1.443%; about 9.6bp over CGB, near its 1-year tight.

adbc:10.note: Down 1.8bp to 1.701%; about 6.7bp over CGB, 3.0bp over CDB; new 10Y sold at 1.6566%.

exim:10.note: Down 1.8bp to 1.692%; about 5.7bp over CGB, 2.0bp over CDB.

watch: Next: wealth-product NAVs and fund flows after Friday's selloff, the US midterms (Nov 3), the RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4), US payrolls (Nov 6), October trade and FX reserves (Nov 7), then October CPI/PPI and credit data and the November MoF and local bond calendars, including RMB150bn of bank-capital special bonds.
